batchName: Empire: The Fall of the West (AD 395-476) - Hard Batch 1
chapterName: Empire: The Fall of the West (AD 395-476)

questions.question: The end of the West in 476 is only a convention. Until what year did a Roman enclave in northern Gaul survive?
questions.explanation: The Roman enclave in northern Gaul lasted until 486. A deposed emperor also kept claiming the throne from Dalmatia until 480.
questions.sourceQuote: A deposed emperor still claimed the throne from Dalmatia, on the Adriatic coast, until 480, and a Roman enclave in northern Gaul lasted until 486.

questions.question: How did the rich senator who seized the throne in 455 effectively declare war on the Vandals?
options: He refused to pay their annual tribute
He executed their envoys in Rome
He sent a fleet to attack Carthage
He seized Vandal merchant ships at Ostia
He broke off a planned royal marriage with them
He allied with the remnants of the Huns
questions.explanation: Cancelling the planned royal marriage amounted to a declaration of war. When the Vandal fleet arrived, he tried to flee and was torn apart by a Roman mob.
questions.sourceQuote: He broke off a planned royal marriage with the Vandals of Carthage, which amounted to declaring war.

questions.question: How did Odoacer reportedly treat the deposed Romulus Augustulus? (select all that apply)
options: He sent him to Constantinople as a hostage
He sent him to live with relatives in Campania
He forced him to become a monk
He spared the boy's life
He kept him on as a puppet co-ruler
He granted him a yearly pension of 6,000 solidi
questions.explanation: Said to have pitied the 16-year-old, Odoacer spared him, paid him a yearly pension and sent him to relatives in Campania, around Naples. Romulus had never been recognised outside Italy.
questions.sourceQuote: Said to have pitied the 16-year-old, Odoacer spared his life, granted him a yearly pension of 6,000 gold coins (*solidi*) and sent him to live with relatives in Campania, the region around Naples.

questions.question: What finally made Alaric abandon negotiations and march on Rome a third time in 410?
options: The emperor executed his Gothic envoys
A Gothic rival ambushed him during peace talks
Vandal fleets cut off his grain supply
Hunnic raiders attacked his camp
His puppet emperor betrayed him to Ravenna
The Senate refused to pay a second ransom
questions.explanation: An ambush by a Gothic rival during peace talks ended Alaric's patience. The year before, he had besieged Rome again and set up, then deposed, a puppet emperor.
questions.sourceQuote: When a Gothic rival ambushed him during peace talks in 410, Alaric gave up on negotiating and marched on Rome for the third time.

questions.question: How did different Christians explain the sack of Rome in 410? (select all that apply)
options: As God's punishment of a proud city
As a sign the end of the world was near
As proof Rome had abandoned its old gods
As a victory for the true faith over paganism
As the result of Christianity sapping old virtues
As a sign Constantinople should rule the West
questions.explanation: Some Christians saw God's punishment softened by mercy, while others thought the end of the world was near. The claims about abandoned gods and sapped virtues came from pagans.
questions.sourceQuote: Some Christians replied that the disaster was God's punishment of a proud city, softened only by his mercy.

questions.question: Many modern historians think the real turning point of Attila's 451 campaign was what?
options: The death of the Visigothic king
Attila's retreat to his camp of wagons
The razing of Aquileia
The fight over the ridge on the Catalaunian Plains
The pope's embassy to Attila
The defence of Orléans by its Alan garrison
questions.explanation: Modern historians often point to the Alans' defence of Orléans rather than the famous battle. They also reject ancient death tolls of up to 300,000 as impossible.
questions.sourceQuote: Ancient death tolls of up to 300,000 are impossible, the main account is distorted, and many think the real turning point was the defence of Orléans.

questions.question: The taxes Rome lost with Africa could have paid for roughly how many infantry?
options: About 4,000
Nearly 40,000
About 10,000
About 20,000
About 100,000
About 200,000
questions.explanation: Africa's lost revenue could have funded nearly 40,000 foot soldiers. The government made up for it by taxing peasants harder while the wealthy avoided paying.
questions.sourceQuote: Its lost taxes could have paid for nearly 40,000 infantry.

questions.question: Which details show that the Gothic sack of 410 was restrained by the standards of the age? (select all that apply)
options: No buildings were damaged by fire
Most monuments survived
The city's two great basilicas served as sanctuaries
The emperors' tombs were left untouched
No citizens were harmed or tortured
There was no general massacre
questions.explanation: There was no general massacre, most monuments survived and the two great basilicas served as refuges. Still, imperial tombs were ransacked, citizens tortured and buildings near the old Senate house burned.
questions.sourceQuote: There was no general massacre, most monuments survived, and the city's two great basilicas served as sanctuaries.

questions.question: What happened right after the West's half-Vandal general was executed in 408?
options: An eastern army was sent to occupy Italy
The Vandals crossed from Spain into Africa
Alaric surrendered and settled in Aquitaine
Soldiers massacred barbarian families; thousands joined Alaric
The court moved its capital back to Milan
Attila crossed the Rhine to avenge his ally
questions.explanation: Roman soldiers massacred the families of barbarian troops, driving thousands into Alaric's arms. The general had been lured out of a church sanctuary and executed on 22 August.
questions.sourceQuote: Roman soldiers then massacred the families of barbarian troops, and thousands fled to join Alaric.

questions.question: By 395, what state was the western Roman army in?
options: Undefeated for half a century
Freshly rebuilt with Hunnic recruits
Stationed almost entirely in Britain
Merged with the eastern army
Bled white by two civil wars
Commanded directly by the Goths
questions.explanation: Two civil wars had drained the western army. At the same time the Goths had become an armed power able to threaten either half of the empire.
questions.sourceQuote: By 395 the Goths were an armed power that could threaten either half of the empire, while the western army had been bled white by two civil wars.
